- Screener query pattern from a public user screen: `Debt to equity < 0.25 AND Return on capital employed > 20% AND Net profit > 200 AND Public holding < 30% AND Pledged percentage < 10%` — [Screener screen "334 to 48 companies >1000 cr mcap"](https://www.screener.in/screens/3679793/334-to-48-companies-1000-cr-mcap/) (as summarised by search; community example, not official docs).
- Public "Coffee Can Investing" Screener screen: starts `Market Capitalization > 1000 AND Average return on capital employed 10Years > 14% ...`; requires avg ROCE > 14% over 10/7/5/3 yrs plus current and previous year, the same for ROE, Debt to equity < 1, sales growth > 9% over 10/7/5/3 yrs and current year, Pledged percentage < 15%; returned ~100 results (4 pages) when fetched Nov 2026 [VERIFY LIVE count] — [Screener: Coffee Can Investing](https://www.screener.in/screens/1125448/coffee-can-investing/)
- Other public quality screens to clone: "Clean-balance-sheet compounders" (D/E < 0.5, ROCE > 18, ROE > 12) — [Screener](https://www.screener.in/screens/3103240/clean-balance-sheet-compounders/); "Consistent Compounders" (ROCE > 20% + low debt) — [Screener](https://www.screener.in/screens/3468167/the-consistent-compounders-screener/); "High Quality Long-Term Compounders" — [Screener](https://www.screener.in/screens/3394399/high-quality-long-term-compounders/); "High ROE, Continuous growth, Low PE, Low Debt" — [Screener](https://www.screener.in/screens/141333/High-Quality-Stocks-with-consistent-growth/?order=asc)
- Tickertape also hosts user-built compounder screens (e.g., "Quality compounders at a low EV/EBITDA") — [Tickertape](https://www.tickertape.in/screener/equity/user/quality-compounders-at-a-low-evebitda-auQCO3-ROu6xsOcX)
- Credit-rating "non-cooperation" and downgrades are a practical early-warning feed: Gensol saw credit downgrades around the April 2025 SEBI interim order — [Business Today](https://businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/sebi-interim-order-gensol-fund-diversion-stock-plunge-credit-downgrades-472172-2025-04-16)

body:
`theme:sector-insurance` · confidence: single-source · tickers: HDFCLIFE, SBILIFE, ICICIPRULI, LICI, ICICIGI, STARHEALTH

**How it makes money:** Life: present value of future profits per policy (VNB) + EV unwind. General: underwriting + float income.

**Metrics that matter:**
- APE growth
- VNB margin & VNB growth
- persistency 13M/61M
- product mix (protection/non-par/ULIP/par)
- Operating RoEV / EV growth
- solvency ratio
- GI: combined ratio, loss ratio

**Value chain and where margins sit:** Manufacturer -> distribution (banca ~50–65% for bank-owned insurers, agency, brokers, online) -> reinsurance. Distribution captures large commissions; protection margins are highest; reinsurers set term-pricing terms.

**Cycle drivers:** Equity market (ULIP), rate cycle (non-par guarantees), tax policy on maturity proceeds, IRDAI product and commission rules, GST changes.

**Lead indicators (public India data):**
- Life Insurance Council / IRDAI monthly new business premium
- GI Council monthly gross direct premium
- Bank partner branch additions
- 10-yr G-sec yield (non-par pricing)

**What separated winners from losers:** Winners: multi-channel distribution, protection-heavy mix, top-quartile persistency, conservative assumptions (low EV variance). Losers: single banca dependency, ULIP-heavy in a falling market, frequent negative EV assumption changes.

**Valuation ranges and peaks/troughs:** P/EV (and implied value of new business multiple). Private life 3–5x EV at the 2017–21 peak, ~2–3x after the Feb 2023 tax change. LIC listed May 2022 at ~1.1x EV and fell well below it. GIs ~25–40x P/E.

**Current state (Nov 2026):** H1 FY27: ICICI Pru Life VNB +22.3% to ₹12.83 bn; HDFC Life VNB +12% with Q1 margin 25% (~60 bps residual GST hit); Bajaj Life H1 margin 19.2% (21.6% pre-₹95 cr GST impact). The GST exemption on individual policies (Sep 2025) helps volumes but removes ITC.

**Classic traps:**
- Valuing on APE growth alone
- EV boosted by assumption changes
- Bank parent cross-sell that reverses (mis-selling crackdowns)
- Ignoring surrender-value and commission regulation
- Health insurers' claim ratio inflation

`case_study:astral-2009-2024` · tickers: ASTRAL · confidence: single-source

Split/bonus-adjusted ₹1.51 (Mar 2009) → ₹2,406 (Jul 2024) ≈1,590x; ₹1,254 on 19 Nov 2026 (−48%). Twin engine: P/E 7.9 → 118 (15x) × implied EPS ~106x. Drawdowns: −85% in 2008 (before the run), then −35%/−36% (2010–11), −34% (2015–16), −49% (Jul 2024–Mar 2025). Early signal (unverified narrative, general knowledge): early Indian CPVC plumbing-pipe player (Lubrizol technology tie-up) as plumbing shifted from galvanised iron to plastic; brand + distributor pull; FY09–11 the stock traded at P/E 9–15 while EPS doubled. Screener shows ROCE 21–29% and low debt through FY15–26. Investors who held from 2009–2013 rode a near-continuous rerating to 60–100x by 2014–2020. Ended/stalled: FY22–FY26 EPS was roughly flat (₹18 → ₹22 TTM) because of PVC price swings, slower adhesives/paints diversification and more competition, yet P/E was still 85–118 in 2023–24; P/E has since compressed to ~57. Lesson: about half the log-return was rerating; when revenue growth fell to ~10% and EPS stalled, a 100x+ multiple halved. Building-material leaders deserve a premium, but not one that assumes 25% growth forever.

Key data: **start_year**: 2009; **end_year**: 2024; **start_price**: 1.51; **end_price**: 2406; **price_nov2026**: 1254; **multiple**: ~1,590x; **pe_start**: 7.9; **pe_end**: 118.4; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~106x; **max_drawdown**: -49% (2024-25); -36% inside run; **early_signals**: category shift GI→CPVC; P/E <15 with EPS doubling (2009-11); **ended**: EPS flat FY22-26 at 85-118x P/E; **lesson**: PE share ~37%; flat EPS at 100x = halving

Sources: <https://www.screener.in/company/ASTRAL/consolidated/>

`case_study:cdsl-2019-2024` · tickers: CDSL · confidence: verified

IPO Jun 2017 at ₹149 (≈₹74.5 after the 2024 1:1 bonus). ₹94 (Aug 2019) → ATH ₹1,943 (Dec 2024) ≈21x; P/E 16.7 → 76 (4.6x) × implied EPS ~4.5x, about 50% rerating. ₹1,423 on 19 Nov 2026 (−27%). Drawdowns: −53% (2017–19), −44% (Jan 2022–Mar 2023), −45% (Dec 2024–Mar 2025). Early signal: depository account counts are public. CDSL went from 1 cr accounts (Sep 2015) to 2 cr (Jan 2020), 3 cr (Jan 2021) and 4 cr (Jul 2021); FY21 added in about four months what FY17 or FY18 added in a year. Q4 FY21 profit ₹51.7 cr vs ₹28.6 cr. In Mar 2020 the stock sat at P/E ~20 while the account curve was going vertical (COVID-era retail inflows, IPO boom). Ended/stalled: account additions and IPO/KYC revenue slowed in 2022, and after the SEBI F&O curbs (late 2024) trading-linked revenue cooled; EPS FY25 ₹25.2 → FY26 ₹21.8. Lesson: a free monthly alt-data series gave a 6–12 month lead, but at 60–76x the multiple already discounted the boom; when the series flattened, half the gain went.

Key data: **start_year**: 2019; **end_year**: 2024; **start_price**: 94.3; **end_price**: 1943; **price_nov2026**: 1423; **multiple**: ~21x; **pe_start**: 16.7; **pe_end**: 76.2; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~4.5x; **max_drawdown**: -44% (2022-23); **early_signals**: demat account counts (public, monthly); **ended**: account-add slowdown; F&O curbs; **lesson**: alt-data lead, but price the boom cyclically

body:
**Hidden trap: GE's smooth earnings, low P/E and dividend** (`case_study:hidden-trap-ge-smooth-earnings`, verified). THE GOOD NUMBER: for years GE delivered steady, predictable earnings that met or beat guidance, a moderate P/E and a long dividend record; the stock was ~$30-32 in mid-2016. WHY IT LIED: earnings that smooth across power turbines, aviation and a finance arm are improbable; GE Capital and accounting choices absorbed volatility. Industrial cash flow was flattered by selling receivables to GE Capital and by 'deferred monetisation' (booking service-contract profits ahead of cash, so contract assets grew faster than revenue); the dividend exceeded free cash flow; a run-off long-term-care insurance book was under-reserved (Jan 2018: $6.2 bn after-tax charge plus ~$15 bn reserve top-ups); Alstom (2015) was bought at the power cycle peak ($22 bn goodwill impairment, Oct 2018). Dividend halved Nov 2017 and cut to $0.01 in 2018; stock ~$6.7 by Dec 2018. TEST: compare reported earnings volatility with what the businesses' cycles imply; dividend cover by FCF; trend of contract assets and factored receivables; ask what long-tail liabilities sit in a finance subsidiary. LESSON: unusually smooth earnings in cyclical businesses are a sign of management, not of quality.

**Hidden trap: Rajesh Exports at 9-20x P/E on Rs 2 lakh cr of revenue** (`case_study:hidden-trap-rajesh-exports-low-pe`, verified). THE GOOD NUMBER: Rajesh Exports looked cheap and solid: trailing P/E mostly 9-20 (screener median ~15), ROCE 17-20% in FY15-17, PAT Rs 1,069-1,292 cr (FY16-19), revenue Rs 1.6-2.6 lakh cr, positive CFO in most years, promoter holding ~54%. Price peaked ~Rs 947 (2022, adjusted). WHY IT LIED (alleged): at operating margins of 0.4-1.1%, profit is a sliver of a revenue figure that is mostly gold passing through; a small mis-statement of revenue or cost moves profit 100%. Disclosure by segment and geography was thin and auditors changed often. SEBI's ex-parte interim order (3 Jun 2026, confirmed Oct 2026) alleged standalone revenue overstated by ~Rs 12,557 cr over FY21-24 and said the forensic auditor was denied ERP and journal access; promoter barred from dealing. Reported OPM fell to ~0.0-0.1% and ROCE to 1-3% (FY24-26); stock ~Rs 48 (20 Nov 2026), about -95% from peak. Allegations are not final findings. TEST: when margin < 2%, value the company on what you can verify (cash returned, dividends, independently confirmed volumes), not on P/E; treat 'cheap' plus opacity plus auditor churn as a trap pattern. LESSON: a low P/E on unverifiable earnings is not a margin of safety.

body:
Annual values from the screener standalone page, fiscal years ≤ FY0 only (year = calendar year of FY0's column
month; columns in a different month — half-year/transition columns — are dropped).
- **(a) A — CFO/PAT 5y < 0.3** (v2 status: question). Σ CFO / Σ PAT over the up-to-5 fiscal years ending FY0, using
  years where both are present; ≥ 3 such years required. Σ PAT ≤ 0 ⇒ unknown (ratio undefined; counted).
  Secondary **A7** < 0.7.
- **(b) B25 — promoter pledge > 25% of promoter holding at T** (v2: graded); **B50 > 50%** (escalation level).
  Source: the latest BSE shareholding-pattern XBRL *filed before T* (normally the June quarter of the snapshot
  year), and only if that quarter ends within 12 months before T. Pledge % = pledged/encumbered promoter shares ÷
  promoter shares (re-derived). A filing that declares "no promoter shares pledged" = 0%. No promoter shares ⇒ 0%
  (not fired). Unknown if no BSE code, no SHP filed in that window, no XBRL, or parse failure (all counted).
  Exploratory: **B_rise** = pledge % at T ≥ pledge % a year earlier + 10 pp (needs the SHP filed ~12 months
  earlier; FY2016's prior-year SHPs mostly have no XBRL, so this is FY2018-only in practice).
- **(c) C — debt growth with negative CFO** (v2: question). Borrowings FY0 ≥ 1.5 × borrowings FY0−3 (from zero:
  fired only if FY0 borrowings > 5% of FY0 sales) **and** Σ CFO FY0−2..FY0 < 0 (all three years present).
- **(d) D50 — other income > 50% of PBT** (v2: question). Σ other income / Σ PBT over FY0−2..FY0 (≥ 2 years),
  Σ PBT > 0; Σ PBT ≤ 0 ⇒ unknown (counted). Secondary **D30** > 30% (the old Part B R5 threshold).
- **(e) E — receivable days up > 50% in 3 years** (v2: graded with counterparty). Debtor days FY0 ÷ debtor days
  FY0−3 > 1.5, with FY0−3 debtor days > 0. Exploratory **E60**: also FY0 debtor days ≥ 60 (removes tiny bases).
- **(f) "Implausible economics" is NOT tested** — lesson L20: a mechanical proxy (ROCE > 40% or OPM +10 pp)
  did not reproduce the judgment rule. It stays judgment-only.
- **ANY** = A ∨ B25 ∨ C ∨ D50 ∨ E; fired if any component fires, not fired only if every component is known and
  none fires, else unknown. Secondary **ANY_np** (without pledge, so coverage does not depend on BSE data) and
  **TWO+** (≥ 2 of the five fire; exploratory).
